I want to evolve my skills and improve my skill library health
Review my skills for debt and look for improvements

Execute skill steroids mutate to improve my agent capabilities
Help me create a new skill for data processing
How do I use skills in Claude Code?

Give me templates for writing professional skills

orchestration.reasoning: This is explicitly a meta-orchestrator that reads other SKILL.md files, dispatches to sub-skills (orchestrator, governor, observer, analyzer, evolver, experimenter, lineage) in sequence, enforces a mandatory governance gate before writes, and persists run artifacts itself, making it a standalone coordinating agent rather than a pure worker.
evidence: "Orchestrates observation, analysis, governance, and governed mutation."

simulations.task: User runs '/skill-steroids' or says 'skill steroids audit' with no scope, wanting a health check of their ~/.claude/skills or project skill library (duplicates, stale descriptions, unused skills, weak triggers).
simulations.expected_output: Claude resolves empty $ARGUMENTS to audit mode, reads evolution.md, then opens orchestrator/SKILL.md and executes from Step 0. Since the orchestrator, observer, analyzer, and principles files are not included in this skill's visible content, actual behavior (what gets scanned, what metrics are computed, report structure) is entirely dependent on those unseen files. Assuming they exist and are well-formed, output would be a markdown report written to .skill-steroids/runs/<run-id>.md summarizing skill inventory, redundancy/overlap findings, and improvement proposals, ending with a request for explicit approval before any file is touched.
simulations.quality_notes: The routing logic itself (table lookup, default-to-audit, run-id persistence) is clear and easy to follow. But this file is a thin dispatcher — nearly all substantive behavior (what 'health' means, what the Observer/Analyzer actually check) lives in files not shown here, so quality of the real output can't be verified from this skill alone and is a single point of failure if any referenced path is missing or renamed in a given install.

simulations.task: User says 'evolve skill git-worktree' wanting the skill improved (e.g., tighter description, clearer trigger phrases) after noticing it doesn't fire reliably.
simulations.expected_output: Matches the table's 'evolve skill X' pattern → mutate mode with scope 'git-worktree'. Claude reads evolution.md and orchestrator/SKILL.md, which presumably routes to Observer (inspect current skill file) → Analyzer (diagnose the triggering issue) → Evolver (draft a revised SKILL.md/description) → Governor (check the proposed diff against principles.md) before presenting anything. Per the Human-in-the-loop section, Claude must stop and ask explicit approval before creating/editing/deleting the skill file, presenting the proposed diff and rationale first, then persisting the run log.
simulations.quality_notes: The explicit 'Never skip Governor before any write' and the Human-in-the-loop approval gate are strong safety design — this is the clearest, most self-contained part of the skill and would reliably prevent silent mutation regardless of what the unseen Evolver/Governor files contain. Weakness: no guidance here on what format the proposed diff should take or how conflicts with principles.md are surfaced to the user, so the user-facing quality of the approval step is unpredictable.

simulations.task: User says 'skill debt' — a phrase listed as a trigger in the frontmatter description but not present in the in-body activation table, expecting an audit-style response focused specifically on technical-debt-like issues (bloat, duplication, abandoned skills).
simulations.expected_output: Best case, Claude infers 'skill debt' maps to audit mode (nearest table entry, 'skill library health') and proceeds as in Task 1. Worst case, the mismatch between the frontmatter's trigger list and the body's table causes hesitation or an incorrect mode guess, since disable-model-invocation:true means this skill won't be auto-selected by semantic matching — it must be invoked directly, and once invoked, the model has to reconcile the ambiguity itself using judgment not covered by the skill's own text.
simulations.quality_notes: This is a real inconsistency: five phrases are advertised as triggers in the description ('skill library health', 'skill debt', 'review my skills', plus the two also in the table) but the body's routing table only lists two rows, omitting 'skill debt' and 'review my skills' entirely. That gap forces the executing model to freelance a mapping the skill never actually specifies, which is a moderate clarity defect for a skill whose whole purpose is deterministic governance/routing.

scope.assessment: As an orchestrator entry point delegating to seven sub-skill components for a full skill-lifecycle governance system, it's coherent in purpose but broad in surface area, spanning observation, analysis, mutation, experimentation, and lineage tracking rather than one tightly-scoped task.
